maria: quick question — we're moving foo-api to an NLB for the edge/internal split. Should we terminate TLS at the LB or pass TLS through to the pods? app speaks gRPC (http2) and we want mTLS between services.

alex: if you require mTLS between services, terminating at ALB will break end-to-end client certs unless you re-establish TLS at the app. ALB is L7 and typically terminates to do routing. NLB can do TCP passthrough so TLS can stay to the pod.

sam: +1 for TLS to the pods for true mTLS. Also easier for cert rotation when apps validate peer certs. For gRPC, terminating at the pod avoids protocol translation issues.

jordan: notes for AWS LB Controller + EKS: you can annotate the service for NLB + TCP healthchecks. Example we use: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: "tcp"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip"
```
Remember to set `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` if you want source IP preserved for pod-level mTLS checks (we do in prod).

maria: we have cert-manager issuing workload certs from Vault CA already, plus a sidecar for reload. Ops concern is healthchecks — will NLB TCP healthchecks play nicely with gRPC health?

sam: use gRPC health on an unencrypted port internally or configure the NLB to do TCP healthchecks against the gRPC port (health probe returns success at TCP layer). Alternatively, add a small HTTP health endpoint on the pod that the NLB can hit via a separate ingress (but that adds complexity). For now TCP healthcheck on port 8080 (grpc) is fine.

maria: plan: NLB TCP passthrough -> TLS to pod; keep `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`; use cert-manager/Vault for cert rotation; configure TCP healthchecks on grpc port. I'll open a PR for the terraform changes (target group health_check, port 8080, tcp). Ping @alex for review.
